advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an empty extracted required_uv as an explicit error (or assert the producer ran) rather than silently skipping the uv mismatch check.
evidence: The negative/empty extraction path (no pyproject, renamed key, different quoting) is indistinguishable from 'uv version matches' — both proceed to `uv venv` with no signal the pin check was bypassed.
advisory.finding: The uv-version mismatch guard fails open: when sed extracts nothing (pyproject.toml missing, moved, or required-version format changed) `required_uv` is empty and `[ -n "$required_uv" ]` silently skips the check, so a repo that CANNOT determine its required uv version behaves identically to one whose uv matches — the guard reports success by producing nothing.
scenarios: pyproject.toml [tool.uv].required-version is renamed/reformatted or absent in a worktree
A future refactor moves the required-version out of the top-level pyproject
advisory.suggested_fix: When required_uv is empty, emit an ERROR that the required-version could not be read from pyproject.toml and exit non-zero, instead of falling through the `-n` guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the expected required uv version from pyproject.toml in the test rather than hardcoding '0.12.7'.
evidence: tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py:184: assert "ERROR: selected uv is version 0.12.9, but this repository requires 0.12.7" in combined
tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py:161 uses `_pinned_version()` for single-sourcing the Python pin — the uv version is not similarly single-sourced.
advisory.finding: The new test hardcodes the literal required uv version '0.12.7' in its assertion instead of deriving it from pyproject.toml, so a legitimate required-version bump breaks this test even when the Makefile logic remains correct — unlike the sibling tests which single-source via `_pinned_version()`.
scenarios: Bumping required-version in pyproject.toml to a new uv release
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a helper that reads required-version from pyproject.toml (mirroring the Makefile sed) and build both the stub uv_version and the expected assertion string from it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the mismatch test's provisioning guard to match the recorded log format (drop the `uv ` prefix), e.g. assert `"venv --python" not in invocation_log.read_text()` — or assert the log file simply does not exist.
evidence: Assertion under review: `assert not invocation_log.exists() or "uv venv --python" not in invocation_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`
Stub logs `$*` only: `printf "%s\n" "$*" >> "{tmp_path}/uv-args.txt"` — for `uv venv --python X .venv` the logged value is `venv --python X .venv`, without the leading `uv`.
Corroborated by test_make_venv_asks_for_the_pinned_interpreter line 161: `assert f"venv --python {_pinned_version()} .venv" in invocation` — the recorded form omits the `uv` prefix.
Regression blindness (criterion d): the intended guard — uv must NOT provision after a version mismatch — cannot fail via this assertion because its substring never matches the recorded log format.
advisory.finding: The mismatch test's guard that uv provisioning did not run is a fail-open assertion: it checks `"uv venv --python" not in invocation_log`, but the uv stub logs `$*` = `venv --python X .venv` with NO leading 'uv' (confirmed by test_make_venv_asks_for_the_pinned_interpreter line 161 asserting `venv --python {version} .venv`). The substring 'uv venv --python' can never appear in the log, so the right-hand side of the OR is always true — even if the Makefile regressed and ran `uv venv --python` after detecting the mismatch, this assertion would still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the substring to match what the stub records: `assert not invocation_log.exists() or "venv --python" not in invocation_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`. Given the mismatch exits before invoking uv, `assert not invocation_log.exists()` alone is the stronger, unambiguous guard.
